definitions.explanation: A person's family name, as opposed to their given name. In Japanese naming order, the surname comes first.

examples.japanese: {姓|せい}と{名|めい}を{書|か}いてください。
examples.english: Please write your surname and given name.

examples.japanese: {結婚|けっこん}して{姓|せい}が{変|か}わった。
examples.english: My surname changed when I got married.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}では{夫婦|ふうふ}が{同|おな}じ{姓|せい}を{名乗|なの}ることが{法律|ほうりつ}で{決|き}められている。
examples.english: In Japan, the law requires married couples to share the same surname.

notes:
USAGE:
{姓|せい} is a formal word for surname. In everyday speech, {名字|みょうじ} or {苗字|みょうじ} is more common. {姓|せい} appears frequently on official forms and in formal writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {姓|せい}と{名|めい} (surname and given name)
- {姓|せい}を{名乗|なの}る (to go by a surname)
- {旧姓|きゅうせい} (maiden name; former surname)
- {夫婦|ふうふ}{別姓|べっせい} (separate surnames for married couples)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{名字|みょうじ} is the everyday equivalent. {氏|し} is used in formal/legal contexts. {姓|せい} falls in between.
